validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: real, well-documented project. Gulf South Pipeline Company, LLC and Texas Gas Transmission, LLC (both Boardwalk Pipelines, LP subsidiaries) filed a formal NGA section 7 certificate application with FERC on 2025-09-12 (Docket Nos. CP25-547-000 / CP25-549-000, pre-filing PF25-6-000 from 2025-02-07) for the Kosciusko Junction Pipeline Project (Boardwalk's Kosci Junction). FERC issued a Notice of Intent to prepare an EIS 2025-11-14, a draft EIS 2026-04-01 (comment period closed 2026-05-26), and a final EIS around 2026-07 (Marcellus Drilling News headline; not independently re-verified beyond the trade-press summary). Boardwalk's board approved FID on 2024-12-11 (PR Newswire 2024-12-16). This is not a GEM-only entity -- the sheet's own eia.gov/data.php citation is a navigation page that never actually names or describes this project, but independent FERC/Federal Register and company-disclosure documents amply confirm it. CLASSIFICATION: correctly recorded as a gas transmission pipeline -- Gulf South is an interstate NGA-jurisdictional transmission pipeline; Fuel=Gas and PipelineType=transmission both confirmed (see fills). DUPLICATE: checked against the 44-row roster, incl. the other three Gulf South rows (P7780 PLUSS, P7784 Eunice Reliability & Lake Charles Supply, P7815 Southeast CURE) -- all are separate, differently-scoped Boardwalk/Gulf South expansion filings; no overlap with Kosci Junction/Kosciusko Junction found. No duplicate. ROUTE: routes-repo geojson (P7810.geojson, 39-pt LineString) runs from ~(-89.55, 32.99) near Kosciusko/Attala County, MS south to ~(-88.80, 31.91) in the Attala-to-Clarke corridor area of central Mississippi -- consistent with the sheet's StartState/Province=Mississippi, EndState/Province=Mississippi and with the FERC filing's Attala-to-Clarke framing. Note for future route work: the FERC filing actually describes TWO separate built segments -- the 103-mile Kosciusko Junction Pipeline mainline (Holmes, Attala, Leake, Newton, Jasper Counties) and a separate 8-mile Columbia Gulf Lateral (Clarke County) -- which this single undifferentiated route feature does not distinguish; not flagged as a mismatch since the sheet's simple Attala->Clarke termini are directionally correct, but a two-segment redigitization would be more accurate. Sources: FERC Federal Register application notice (2025-09-30, verified, names project), bwpipelines.com project page (verified, names project), PGJ 2025-12-16 article (verified, names project).

validity.recommendation: update Capacity to ~1,175 MMcf/d (the FERC-application design/firm capacity) from the recorded 1,500
validity.researcher_notes: Sheet records Capacity=1500.00 MMcf/d, cited (per the existing_ref_check) to eia.gov/naturalgas/data.php -- a navigation page that does not contain this figure. Every primary source found states a materially different number: (1) FERC's Federal Register notice of the formal application (filed 2025-09-12; verified, names the project) -- 'The Project will create approximately 1.175 billion cubic feet per day (Bcf/d) of new pipeline capacity, of which 1.1 Bcf/d is subscribed to Southern Company Services, Inc., Florida Power & Light Company, and PowerSouth Energy Cooperative.' (2) Natural Gas Intel, 2026-06-22 (verified) -- 'full 1.175 Bcf/d project capacity available in July 2028.' (3) Boardwalk's own project page (verified) and the 2024-12-16 PR Newswire FID release (verified) -- 'Designed for up to 1.16 billion cubic feet per day (Bcf/d) ... with potential expansion to 1.58 Bcf/d' (the 1.16-1.18 range is the as-designed/firm capacity; 1.58 Bcf/d is a forward-looking expansion ceiling, not the base project capacity). None of these near 1,500. The EIA Jul-2025 pre-filing-era release (the 'strong' EIA candidate quoting 1500 MMcf/d, docket PF25-6-000) appears to be the sheet's original source and is a stale early estimate superseded by the formal FERC application's 1.175 Bcf/d figure (also matched by EIA's own later Aug-2026 release, 1180 MMcf/d). Recommend correcting to 1175.00 MMcf/d (or noting the 1160-1580 range if a single point value is undesirable). See paired fill on Capacity [ref].

validity.recommendation: review StartYear1 (currently 2029) against the accelerated, more current in-service timeline -- partial service as early as 2028
validity.researcher_notes: Sheet's StartYear1=2029 was cited (dead link, see fill) to a bwpipelines KOSCI-Project page that 404s. That figure traces to the original 2024-12-16 FID press release, which targeted 'first half of 2029' in-service. Two more current, independent primary sources show the timeline has since been accelerated: Boardwalk's live project page (verified, accessed 2026-09; General Project Timeline) states 'Partial In-Service: As early as April 2028' and 'Full In-Service: September 2028.' Natural Gas Intel, 2026-06-22 (verified), reports Gulf South's own June 12 notice: interim flows of up to 630 MMcf/d beginning April 2028, full 1.175 Bcf/d project capacity available July 2028, with the interim arrangement running until 2029-04-01 when full contracted volumes take over. So the pipeline is now expected to begin physical service in 2028, with full contractual subscription by all committed shippers not until 2029 -- the sheet's single StartYear1=2029 conflates the two. Recommend StartYear1=2028 (partial in-service, April) as the primary value, with the 2029 full-subscription date noted in ResearcherNotes/StartYear2 if the schema supports staged start years. Not treated as a Status verdict='change' in status_reviews below because the recorded Status ('proposed') is still correct -- construction has not yet started as of 2026-09.

validity.recommendation: review ConstructionYear (currently 2028) -- Boardwalk's own timeline gives a 2027-2028 construction window, i.e. construction is expected to START in 2027
validity.researcher_notes: Sheet's ConstructionYear=2028 was cited (dead link, see fill) to the same 404'd bwpipelines KOSCI-Project page. Boardwalk's current live project page (verified) gives a 'General Project Timeline' of 'Regulatory Review: 2025-2026' then 'Construction: 2027-2028' -- i.e., construction is expected to begin in 2027 (to meet the April 2028 partial in-service target above), not start in 2028. This is a single-source figure (Boardwalk's own timeline graphic); I searched NGI, PGJ, and the Federal Register DEIS/FEIS notices for a more precise construction-start date and found only the general 2027-2028 window and an environmental-review completion target of ~2026-12 (FAST-41 dashboard, per NGI) -- no second source states a specific construction-start year. Tier medium accordingly. Flagging as a spec concern rather than a hard correction given the imprecision. The FINDING is unchanged; only the confidence claim was wrong.
